messages_body:
Hi Karthik,

Quick one from procurement: attached is PO 43928. Our AP team requires the PO referenced on the invoice header exactly as "PO: 43928 / GL-PR-22" and the invoice to be submitted on a monthly statement run (cutoff the 5th of each month). They also flagged that Greenleaf pays Net60 by default, and we need to confirm whether Redwood can accept Net60 or if there is a path to agree Net45 for the first two months while billing normalizes.

A couple of constraints from our side:
- Single invoice per PO preferred (no split invoices) unless explicitly allowed in the PO metadata.
- The PO must include the contract ID (MSA-2027) in the invoice description for ERP matching.
- If Redwood wants earlier payment terms, we need written approval from Treasury (I can escalate).

Can you confirm whether you can: (1) include the contract ID on invoices, (2) support the exact PO string on invoice header, and (3) whether there's flexibility on Net terms / a short Net45 bridge?

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Shaw
Procurement Manager, Greenleaf Systems

Attachment: Greenleaf_PO_43928.pdf

Ethan — thanks for the clear ask and the PO.

Short answers:
1) We can ensure the invoice header contains "PO: 43928 / GL-PR-22" and add the contract ID MSA-2027 in the description field.
2) On split invoices — our billing system prefers a single invoice per PO but we can emit multiple invoices if you set the PO to allow multi-invoice billing. Is that something Procurement can toggle?
3) Net terms — our standard enterprise terms are Net30, but for strategic bookings we sometimes accept Net45 or Net60 depending on credit and deal economics. For DL-5391 (this engagement) we can offer Net45 for the first 60 days as a bridge if Greenleaf will sign the MSA amendment (attached) and commit to monthly statements. Alternatively, we can offer a 1% early-payment discount if Greenleaf agrees Net30.

Next steps proposed:
- Vanessa to confirm accounting impact and accept or decline the 1% early-pay discount.
- We will sign and return the MSA amendment if that unlocks Net45 bridge.

Ben (cc'd) — any operational caveats for label formats or invoice splitting?

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_amendment_v2.docx

Karthik / Ethan — looping in AP ops notes.

Ben here. A few practicals for ERP matching if you decide to go the Net45-bridge path:
- Our invoicing engine accepts a "PO string" field and a free-text "contract" field. To avoid manual tickets, the PO string must match exactly (case-sensitive).
- If Greenleaf wants multiple invoices per PO, we require each invoice to include an incremental sequence suffix (e.g., PO 43928-1, PO 43928-2) and a cover summary file listing transactions per invoice. That adds manual reconciliation work for our AR team and may delay payment processing by 2–3 business days per additional invoice.
- For the early-pay 1% discount: we'll need a signed amendment that calls out the discount cadence and the invoice net due date to process automatically.

From an operational perspective, Net45 bridge is fine provided the amendment is signed and the PO metadata allows "multi-invoice: false" (i.e., single invoice). If Greenleaf insists on Net60, we will accept it but ask for compressed billing (monthly statements) and a 30-day SLA on disputed items to avoid long-tail receivables.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Karthik / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from Procurement / AP: 

1) We can set the PO to allow multiple invoices, but prefer single invoice. We'll set "multi-invoice: allowed" for PO 43928 to give Redwood flexibility, but sequence suffixes are mandatory for split invoices.
2) Greenleaf Treasury is willing to approve a Net45 bridge for the first 60 days provided Redwood signs the MSA amendment and accepts the 30-day dispute SLA. I'll share the Treasury approval memo after I confirm with our legal counsel.
3) Regarding the 1% early-pay discount — our VP Finance is open but prefers the Net45 bridge to keep cash runway predictable. 

We have DocuSign routing in progress for the MSA amendment (link above). Can Redwood sign the amendment and confirm final invoice header example so AP can pre-configure ERP mapping? Example we need: 

Invoice header line 1: Redwood Inference, Inc.
Invoice header line 2: PO: 43928 / GL-PR-22
Invoice description: Services under MSA-2027; invoice period May 1–31, 2028

If you can confirm the exact sample and sign the DocuSign by EOD Friday, we'll schedule the payment-run mapping for June.

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Shaw
Procurement Manager, Greenleaf Systems
